title: The 6/5 integrality gap for 2-edge-connected spanning multigraphs
credit: '6/5 conjecture' of Alexander, Boyd and Elliott-Magwood (2006); restated in Boyd–Fu–Sun (2016) and Boyd et al. (2020).
premise_risks: Less famous than the TSP 4/3 question; scorer may view it as a sibling of the TSP subtour problem
The '6/5 conjecture' is attributed to its authors but named by its number, not a person
plain: Given nonnegative edge costs on a complete graph, find the cheapest multiset of edges (each edge may be used twice) such that every cut is crossed at least twice, i.e. the result is 2-edge-connected. The LP relaxation only asks for fractional edge weights crossing every cut with total at least 2. Is the best integral solution always within a factor 6/5 of the LP optimum? The factor 6/5 is known to be needed, while the best proven bound is only 3/2 minus a tiny constant.
math: Let $n\ge2$, $c\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{E(K_n)}$ and $x\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{E(K_n)}$ with $x(\delta(S))\ge2$ for all $\emptyset\ne S\subsetneq[n]$. Prove that there is $z\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{E(K_n)}$ with $z(\delta(S))\ge2$ for all such $S$ and $c^\top z\le\tfrac65\,c^\top x$. (Since examples with ratio arbitrarily close to $6/5$ are known, this would show the integrality gap of the cut LP for 2-edge-connected multigraphs is exactly $6/5$.)
